A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PnP-Flow research, with matching authors, core algorithm, and substantial shared experiments. Their text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison. Internal reporting inconsistencies in v2 do not prevent identifying the changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original image-restoration results and computational measurements in Tables 1–4, together with appendix experiments on Dirichlet latents, initialization sensitivity, and rectified flows.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds perceptual-metric evaluations, diffusion-baseline comparisons, Laplace-noise experiments, and blind-restoration examples.

M1.justification: The denoiser and core Algorithm 3 remain unchanged. Appendix A.14 adds a procedural extension for blind restoration: image updates alternate with Adam updates of an unknown blur kernel, and a related example jointly estimates a masking operator.

E1.justification: Appendices A.11 and A.14 add Laplace-corrupted CelebA super-resolution and blind deconvolution and masking examples. These substantially extend the evaluated noise and operator-knowledge regimes. CelebA, AFHQ-Cat, CelebA-HQ, and Simplex-MNIST coverage already existed in v1; no new dataset is introduced.

E2.justification: Tables 10–11 add evaluated DDRM and DPS baselines across four restoration tasks on both main datasets. This substantially broadens diffusion comparisons beyond the existing PnP-Diff baseline. The original flow-based and PnP comparisons remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds LPIPS evaluation and a 100-image Laplace super-resolution protocol with 2× downsampling and noise levels 0.1 and 0.3. Blind tests introduce unknown operators, with known kernel size and a shared kernel across channels. Existing Gaussian protocols remain stated as before. Table 7's CelebA 4× header conflicts with 2× elsewhere and does not reliably establish a changed setting.

E4.justification: Appendix A.9 and Figure 13 add a case visualization separating gradient, interpolation, and denoising outputs. Appendix A.14 adds exploratory blind-restoration case studies. Existing initialization, Dirichlet-latent, and rectified-flow analyses remain; no systematic component-removal ablation is added.

E5.justification: Both versions state that experiments were seeded and report averages over test images, without introducing confidence intervals, repeated-run variability, or significance tests. Averaging five interpolation realizations remains an algorithmic operation, not new uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v2 adds LPIPS, Laplace-noise, DDRM/DPS, and blind-restoration outcomes. Table 9 reports PnP-Flow PSNRs of 30.30 and 26.50 dB at the two Laplace noise levels. Table 11 newly shows DPS exceeding PnP-Flow on AFHQ-Cat super-resolution PSNR, 27.83 versus 26.75 dB. Existing reconstruction scores are retained, but degraded super-resolution PSNR/SSIM changes from 7.527/0.012 to 10.17/0.182 in Table 1 and from 10.74/0.042 to 11.59/0.216 in Table 2.

T1.justification: Proposition 4 adds the assumption that the latent distribution has bounded support. Appendix A.2 explicitly handles bounded iteration-dependent noise and removes an erroneous extra factor of (1−t_n) from the increment identity. These are substantive but localized corrections; Proposition 1 and its proof remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central PnP/flow-matching contribution, efficiency claims, and main PSNR/SSIM claims remain. The conclusion modestly extends the explicit contribution scope by reporting preliminary Laplace-noise results and promising blind-inverse-problem applications.

C2.justification: Appendix A.10 newly interprets mixed LPIPS rankings through the perception–distortion tradeoff, extending v1's general oversmoothing discussion. New passages clarify likelihood requirements, restrictions of the blind examples, and the bounded-noise assumption. The conclusion also explicitly identifies posterior sampling as a future extension.

D1.justification: v2 newly reports PnP-Flow integration into DeepInv and documents DDRM/DPS checkpoint use and hyperparameter search grids in A.13. A.14 specifies Adam and operator constraints for the blind variant. Existing training details and the hyperparameter values in Tables 5–6 are retained.

R1.justification: Section 4 and new Appendix A.12 substantially expand positioning relative to diffusion approaches. v2 removes the assertion that the listed works are the only generative-model PnP methods, discusses Garber and Tirer, explicitly acknowledges similarity to He et al., and connects the method to decoupled posterior-sampling and null-space approaches. Cheng et al. is also credited for a related interpolation idea.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order remain. Changes include localized introduction and conclusion edits, shorter captions, expanded acknowledgements, an acceptance header, consolidation of existing appendix material, and additional appendix subsections. The retained narrative is not extensively rewritten.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 7–11 and Figures 13–17, covering perceptual evaluation, new comparisons, intermediate algorithm outputs, and new restoration scenarios. Figure 7 gains another example. Existing benchmark and hyperparameter tables are regrouped, and Figure 2 is resized. These substantially expand the visual presentation while retaining earlier displays.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves correctness and critical evaluation: it repairs a missing convergence assumption and algebraic error, adds perceptual assessment beyond v1's distortion metrics, and evaluates additional diffusion baselines that expose performance limitations. Expanded related work also clarifies novelty. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, including Table 7's conflicting downsampling label and disagreement between main and appendix degraded-image scores. The indirect FFHQ-trained diffusion comparisons and qualitative-only blind examples still limit the strength of the added evidence.
